messages:
maya: Heads-up — we're seeing a sharp throughput sag on dedicated-gpu-pool-2 since ~07:10 UTC. +20% tail latency and lots of worker restarts.
raj: seeing same. kernel fallback to generic path and a handful of GPU OOMs reported.
sasha: logs look like rapid slab churn on KV cache, lots of evict churn. sample log:```[2026-03-18T07:11:02Z] worker-143: AllocatorError: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
[2026-03-18T07:11:02Z] worker-143: kv_cache.evicted=312, kv_swap_in_latency_ms=78```
alan: interesting — batching spikes at the same time? our batcher shows sudden increase in max_batch_size from 8->32 on the same host.
taylor: could be bad heuristic when kernel fallback increases per-request memory; batching then multiplies live KV pages.
maya: ops-bot, drop node 10 from pool to stop noisy neighbor while we triage? :skull:
ops-bot: @maya noted. cordoning node ip-10-4-7-10 and draining in progress.
raj: quick profiling dump attached, I pulled pprof on runtime: top shows heavy allocator hot paths in cuMallocRetry and hot kernel selection loop.
sasha: kv-hit-rate was stable until 07:09 then oscillated. evict pressure went from 0.2->0.8 in ~30s. suspect a regression in kv eviction heuristics.
alan: rollback candidate: revert commit a1b2c3d (heuristic tweak for aggressive prefetch). That landed ~06:50 and spike aligns.
taylor: can we patch to cap batcher.max_size=16 and set kv_eviction_aggressiveness=high as temporary mitigations?
maya: yes, apply config patch to cluster: `rdctl apply --pool dedicated-gpu-pool-2 --set batcher.max_size=16 --set kv.eviction=aggressive`
eng-oncall-bot: deploy started: rollout/rb-3847 to dedicated-gpu-pool-2 (2 regions) by maya.
raj: after cap, worker restarts dropped and throughput recovering but still ~8% below baseline. more memfrag likely remains.
sasha: running small script to force KV compaction on the node and monitor fragmentation histogram.```#!/bin/bash
echo compact > /sys/runtime/kv_control
# wait for sweep
sleep 30
cat /proc/runtime/kv_frag_hist```
alan: note: kernel selector also falls back to generic kernels when contiguous GPU memory under threshold; that increases transient allocations — we should consider adding a graceful kernel downgrade that reduces batch size automatically.
taylor: filing follow-up perf task: PERF-912 (investigate allocator + kernel selector interplay, add auto-throttle batching).
maya: summary/action items: 1) cordon noisy node (done), 2) config patch to cap batch size + aggressive eviction (rolling), 3) force KV compaction on impacted nodes, 4) revert heuristic commit a1b2c3d if recovery stalls, 5) perf task PERF-912 for long-term fix.
sasha: logs/trace links: https://logs.redwood.company/streams/cluster/dedicated-gpu-pool-2/2069123456 (scrubbed)
raj: bumping priority to P0 for perf task until we land kernel selector fix.
taylor: will start a small canary with quantized model variant to see unit memory per request drop. canary id: canary/2069-q1
maya: thanks all. keep thread updates here. :thumbsup:
